Pest Control for Stink Bugs — Prevention & Removal Guide

By Shaw's Pest Control  ·  Wichita, KS

How Do You Get Rid of Stink Bugs in Your Home?

If you've noticed shield-shaped brown bugs clustering around your windows or smelled that distinct, unpleasant odor when you vacuum them up, you're dealing with stink bugs. These invasive pests become a serious nuisance across Kansas every fall, and pest control for stink bugs requires a different approach than typical household insects. Shaw's Pest Control has been helping Wichita-area homeowners since 1987, and our Three State Certifications and Master Tech Certification mean we've seen every variation of stink bug invasion imaginable. This guide explains why stink bugs target your home, how to prevent large-scale infestations, and when DIY methods won't cut it anymore.

Why Stink Bugs Invade Kansas Homes in Fall

Stink bugs don't reproduce indoors or cause structural damage, but they're looking for one thing as temperatures drop: a warm place to overwinter. The brown marmorated stink bug, the most common species in Kansas, is an invasive pest from Asia that hitched a ride to the U.S. in the late 1990s. Without natural predators here, their populations explode.

When daytime temperatures dip into the 50s and 60s—typically late September through October in our region—stink bugs begin seeking shelter. They're attracted to sun-warmed exterior walls, especially south and west-facing sides of homes. Once they find cracks around windows, door frames, siding gaps, or utility penetrations, they release an aggregation pheromone that signals other stink bugs to follow.

What starts as a few bugs on your siding can become hundreds clustering inside wall voids, attics, and living spaces. They're not feeding or breeding indoors—they're essentially hibernating—but their sheer numbers and that notorious defensive odor make them one of the most complained-about pests we handle during fall months.

How to Prevent Stink Bug Infestations

The most effective pest control for stink bugs happens before they get inside. Once they've entered wall voids by the hundreds, removal becomes significantly harder.

Seal entry points in late summer. Walk your home's exterior in August and early September. Use weatherproof caulk on cracks around window frames, door trim, and where utilities enter the building. Check soffit vents, gable vents, and chimney caps for gaps. Stink bugs can flatten their bodies to squeeze through surprisingly small openings—anything larger than 1/8 inch is an invitation.

Apply exterior barrier treatments. Professional pest control in Wichita focuses on preventive perimeter treatments before migration season peaks. We apply residual insecticides to foundation walls, around windows and doors, and along eaves where stink bugs first land. These treatments create a barrier that kills bugs on contact before they can signal others or find entry points. Timing matters—treatments work best in mid-to-late September, just as stink bugs begin their search for overwintering sites.

Reduce exterior attractants. Trim vegetation away from your home's exterior walls. Stink bugs congregate on plants before moving to structures, so keeping bushes and tree branches at least two feet from siding reduces staging areas. Remove leaf litter and debris from around your foundation—these provide temporary shelter during their search.

Don't crush them indoors. If stink bugs do make it inside, resist the urge to smash them. That smell is a defensive chemical they release, and it's exactly as unpleasant as the name suggests. Use a vacuum with a bag you can immediately dispose of outside, or knock them into a container of soapy water.

When to Call Professional Pest Control for Stink Bugs

DIY prevention works well for minor intrusions—a few bugs here and there that you can manually remove. But if you're seeing more than a dozen stink bugs per day inside your home, or if you notice clusters on your exterior walls numbering in the hundreds, you're facing an infestation that requires professional pest control intervention.

Here's why: stink bugs already inside your walls will emerge sporadically throughout winter and early spring whenever indoor heat warms the wall voids. You can't effectively treat them yourself once they're hidden in structural spaces. Professional treatments target both active bugs and their harboring sites with products homeowners can't access.

Cost varies based on home size and infestation severity, but most perimeter treatments range from $150–$300 and provide season-long protection when applied at the right time. That investment pays for itself quickly compared to months of dealing with daily invasions and the potential need for multiple interior treatments if the problem goes unchecked.

The best time to call is late August through mid-September—before the migration begins in earnest. Once stink bugs have already moved into wall voids, treatment becomes remedial rather than preventive, requiring different techniques and often multiple service visits.

Stink Bug Problems in the Wichita Area

Wichita's mix of urban neighborhoods and agricultural surroundings creates ideal conditions for stink bug populations. They thrive in soybeans, corn, and fruit trees during summer, then migrate en masse to nearby homes when those food sources dry up in fall. Older homes with original siding and windows tend to have more entry points, but we've treated brand-new construction too—any structure offers what stink bugs need to survive winter.

If you're in Andover, Derby, or any surrounding community, you've likely noticed the problem intensifying over the past decade as stink bug populations have established themselves across Kansas. The good news: consistent preventive treatments dramatically reduce the number of bugs that make it indoors. We've worked with homeowners who went from vacuuming up 50+ stink bugs daily to seeing only a handful per month after implementing a professional barrier program.

Frequently Asked Questions

What attracts stink bugs to my house?

Stink bugs are attracted to warmth and light as temperatures drop in fall. South and west-facing exterior walls that absorb sunlight become gathering points. They're not drawn to food, moisture, or debris like many pests—they're simply seeking protected spaces to overwinter, and your home's wall voids and attic provide ideal shelter.

Do stink bugs bite or cause damage?

No, stink bugs do not bite people or pets, and they don't reproduce or feed indoors. They don't damage structures, furniture, or fabrics. Their only real threat is the foul odor they emit when threatened or crushed, and the nuisance of having dozens or hundreds emerging into living spaces throughout winter months.

Can I get rid of stink bugs myself?

You can manage small numbers by sealing entry points, manually removing visible bugs, and using soapy water traps. However, large infestations—especially once bugs are inside wall voids—require professional pest control for stink bugs. Over-the-counter sprays often just scatter them deeper into structural spaces rather than eliminating the problem.

When is stink bug season in Kansas?

Stink bug activity peaks from mid-September through October when cooling temperatures trigger their search for overwintering sites. You'll see them congregating on exterior walls during warm afternoons. A second wave of activity occurs in March and April when warming temperatures cause overwintering bugs to become active and attempt to exit structures.

How do pest control companies treat for stink bugs?

Professional treatments focus on exterior barrier applications using residual insecticides around the home's perimeter, particularly entry points and sun-exposed walls where stink bugs congregate. We apply these treatments in late summer before migration begins. For existing infestations, interior treatments may include targeted applications in wall voids and attic spaces where bugs are harboring.

Will stink bugs come back every year?

Yes, stink bugs will attempt to return to the same overwintering sites year after year if conditions remain favorable. The aggregation pheromone they release can persist, signaling future generations to target the same structures. Annual preventive treatments in late summer break this cycle by eliminating bugs before they can establish and signal others.

Ready to Stop Stink Bugs Before They Move In?

The best defense against stink bug invasions is a professional barrier treatment applied before fall migration begins. Shaw's Pest Control has protected Wichita-area homes from these persistent pests since 1987, using targeted treatments that stop bugs at the exterior rather than dealing with them room by room all winter long.

Our family-owned team brings honest, no-pressure service and the expertise that comes with Master Tech Certification. We'll assess your home's vulnerable areas, seal what we can, and create a protective barrier that keeps stink bugs—and their smell—outside where they belong.

Call (316) 251-9461 or visit our pest control services page to schedule your pre-season treatment. The best time to act is now—before you're vacuuming bugs every morning.
